Compute career transitions

compute_transition.Rd

Counts, for each reference date, how many entities moved from one group to another since the previous date, and what share of the origin group they make up.

Usage

compute_transition(data, ...)

# S3 method for class 'data.frame'
compute_transition(
  data,
  id_col = "personnel_id",
  group_col,
  drop_duplicates = FALSE,
  across_separations = FALSE,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'tbl_dbi'
compute_transition(
  data,
  id_col = "personnel_id",
  group_col,
  drop_duplicates = FALSE,
  across_separations = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

data

Data frame or remote database table (tbl_dbi) with a ref_date column, the identifier column and the grouping column.

...

Arguments passed to methods.

id_col

Character. Column identifying whose career is tracked, such as a person or a contract. Default "personnel_id".

group_col

Character. Column defining a group, such as a paygrade or a department. To track a combination of groups, such as paygrade within department, combine them into one column beforehand (e.g., paste(paygrade, department, sep = "|")).

drop_duplicates

Logical. Drop every entity with more than one record on the same ref_date, with a warning, so that each entity belongs to a single group per period. Default FALSE, which keeps entities belonging to several groups at once. See Details.

across_separations

Logical. Count moves made across a separation, i.e. between the groups an entity held before leaving the public sector and those it holds on its return. Default FALSE, which treats the return as the start of a new career. See Details.

Value

A table with one row per from, to and ref_date, containing:

transitions

Number of moves from from to to dated ref_date, as detected by detect_transition().

transition_rate

transitions divided by the headcount in from on the previous date in the data, as in compute_movement().

A data.table for data frame input; a lazy table for tbl_dbi input (use dplyr::collect() to bring it into memory).

Details

Moves are found and dated as in detect_transition(), so an entity holding several groups moves from each group it held to each group it joins.

The headcount is the number of distinct entities in each group on each date, from count_entity(), so each entity counts once in every group it holds. It is counted on the same records as the moves: rows with a missing identifier or group, and with drop_duplicates = TRUE the entities dropped as duplicates, are left out of both.

With across_separations = TRUE, a move can span dates on which the entity is missing, but transition_rate still divides by the headcount on the previous date in the data, which such an entity is not part of.

See also

detect_transition(), which finds each move. compute_movement(), which counts hires and separations.

Examples

careers <- data.frame(
  personnel_id = c("a", "a", "a", "b", "b", "b", "b"),
  ref_date = as.Date(c(
    "2020-01-01", "2021-01-01", "2022-01-01",
    "2020-01-01", "2020-01-01", "2021-01-01", "2021-01-01"
  )),
  paygrade = c("G1", "G1", "G2", "A", "B", "A", "C")
)
compute_transition(careers, group_col = "paygrade")
#>      from     to   ref_date transitions transition_rate
#>    <char> <char>     <Date>       <int>           <num>
#> 1:      A      C 2021-01-01           1               1
#> 2:      B      C 2021-01-01           1               1
#> 3:     G1     G2 2022-01-01           1               1
